requirements.requirement: node1 configured to route traffic between lan-a and lan-b (interfaces addressed, IP forwarding enabled)
requirements.summary: node1's VyOS eth1 (lan-a) and eth2 (lan-b) were addressed 10.60.0.1/24 and 10.60.1.1/24 via committed and saved VyOS config, applied through Ansible raw tasks; ip_forward=1 was verified both before and as part of the playbook. Configuration was confirmed present after a full node1 reboot (interfaces and forwarding recovered from saved config).

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other directly on any port through node1
requirements.summary: End-to-end TCP connectivity was demonstrated across node1's routing path on ICMP, SSH (22), and two arbitrary ports (5555, 6666 via HTTP server), both before and after all four nodes were rebooted. Host firewalld rules on node2/node3 (opened via the same Ansible playbook) were a necessary supporting change since the host firewall, not node1, was independently blocking non-allowlisted ports.

requirements.requirement: Original source addresses preserved (no NAT) for cross-subnet traffic
requirements.summary: No NAT/masquerade rules were configured on node1. A tcpdump capture on node1's eth2 during cross-subnet ICMP traffic showed unmodified source IP 10.60.0.2, and an HTTP server access log on node3 recorded the client's original source IP 10.60.0.2 for TCP traffic from node2, directly confirming source-address preservation.

An Ansible inventory and playbook on the node4 control node configure node1's VyOS interfaces and node2/node3's static IPs, routes, and firewall rules. Multiple full playbook runs (including a clean post-restart run) show changed=0 on repeat, demonstrating a declarative, idempotent Ansible implementation rather than ad hoc one-off commands.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (node1-node4)
requirements.summary: All four nodes show a pre-restart boot-identity/health baseline, a restart acknowledgement, a distinct post-restart boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state: node1 (01e92881→32b6a13e, interfaces/forwarding/ping recovered), node2 (254597f8→2fcaacc0, static IP/route/firewall/ping recovered), node3 (2b19e976→4b6bf351, same set recovered), node4 (e796da36→94c1336f, Ansible tooling and SSH access intact, full idempotent playbook re-run succeeded). These boot-id transitions are corroborated by the fixed before-prepare and after-executor lifecycle snapshots.

overall_summary: The executor configured node1 (VyOS) as a transit router between lan-a and lan-b entirely via an Ansible playbook run from the node4 control node, with no NAT configured. Cross-subnet connectivity between node2 and node3 on arbitrary ports (22, 5555, 6666, plus ICMP) was directly verified with tcpdump and application-level logs confirming unmodified source addresses, both before and after a full reboot of all four managed nodes. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was completed for every node with clear pre/post boot-identity transitions, acknowledgements, and recovered state, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Operational hygiene is good: temporary discovery and verification artifacts were mostly cleaned up, with only trivial leftover reboot-log files as residue.
limitations: The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare phase disabled for this task), so preparer-vs-executor state could not be independently distinguished beyond the single before/after-executor comparison provided.

Playbook development involved several failed intermediate ansible-playbook runs due to VyOS raw-command/shell syntax issues (e.g. cmd-6d512a44ced64978, cmd-2d4bf12c6ce3404a); these are treated as normal iterative corrections rather than unrelated experiments since each directly informed the final working playbook.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map clearly to task prerequisites (discovering NIC-to-network pairing via temporary `ip addr add` on node2/node3, cmd-e284b5bcce18460d and cmd-f0bee7f752394cce, later fully superseded by the Ansible-managed nmcli config), Ansible/SSH access setup, iterative playbook fixes for VyOS raw-command syntax (legitimate corrective iterations, not unrelated experiments), and bounded verification tooling (tcpdump, nc, python http.server) that was cleaned up after use (cmd-2acdd3b4e1614775, cmd-95b1a510d932440d). The only residue observed in the after-executor snapshot is a trivial leftover /tmp/reboot.log on node2, node3, and node4 from the reboot-scheduling one-liners (cmd-f402121f60cb47b2, cmd-b325d044018948c1, cmd-4cc5b805b2764f22) that was never cleaned up; this is low-risk, non-security-relevant residue rather than a substantive mutation.
